content.text: {"conditions":{"rc1":{"status":"review","note":"The path from IR-cited affidavits to the prima facie, legitimate-reason, and pretext findings is largely traceable, but the claims list is garbled (the 'Additionally... 2... 3' enumeration lacks a clear item 1), and several reasons the decision relies on (HR guidance requiring a PIP, counseling for attire, two subordinates also asked for notes) are not shown in the summarized evidence, while S2 attributes the rating change to insufficient documentation."},"rc2":{"status":"review","note":"Most characterizations carry IR page cites (e.g., IR 73-74, 82-87, 91, 213, 424), but the final decision's key justifications (HR PIP guidance, attire counseling, comparator subordinates, the one-day-per-week COVID policy) are attributed only to S1 statements without IR citations or documentary sources."},"rc3":{"status":"review","note":"Incident dates are given (June 2020 rating, August 20, 2020 HR email, March 4, 12, and 18, 2021, physician note of March 4, 2021), but the grievance date, EEO contact and complaint filing dates, the bases as filed, and the date of the final agency decision are absent."},"rc4":{"status":"review","note":"The decision is identified as a final agency decision under 29 C.F.R. § 1614.110(b) and applies the prima facie, legitimate nondiscriminatory reason, and pretext framework, but no deciding official is named and there is no indication that conflicting evidence was weighed, such as S2's documentation rationale versus HR guidance or the favorable colleague statements at IR 124 and 128."},"rc5":{"status":"review","note":"The record is substantially cited and lets an independent reviewer follow most of the analysis, but the uncited and internally inconsistent justifications, missing procedural dates, unclear enumeration of claims and bases, and the absence of comparator evidence behind the 'similarly situated' finding leave the conclusion only partly verifiable without outside context."}}}
